conjunction.title: The Conjunction

rows.t: Two planets act as one; you feel their blend constantly.
You may struggle to tell the two energies apart within you.
Under transit, it tends to open a new cycle of experience.
It concentrates focus; you may pour yourself fully into one area.
Its tone depends on the planets; it can soothe or intensify.
You may not notice it, because it simply feels like you.

conjunction.bridge: A conjunction is a meeting, not a measurement.
story: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos names four figures between signs.
Opposition, trine, square, sextile: shapes in the circle.
The conjunction is not one of those figures.
It was treated as a bodily joining, not a line of sight.
Hellenistic authors spoke of planets present together.
Two lights in one place, blending their natures.
conjunction.close: Where two meet, a new beginning tends to form.

sextile.title: The Sextile

rows.t: It offers opportunities, but tends to ask you to act.
You connect two areas of life with natural, friendly ease.
Conversations and contacts may open doors when you reach out.
Its gifts are subtle; you may overlook them without attention.
Under transit, small efforts tend to bring encouraging results.
Too much comfort can leave its promise unused; take one step.

sextile.bridge: A sextile knocks softly; you choose to open.
story: Ptolemy counts the sextile among his four configurations.
Sixty degrees: one sixth of the circle, signs two apart.
Same-gender signs: fire with air, earth with water.
He called it harmonious, a gentler kin of the trine.
Its figure is the hexagon traced inside the zodiac.
sextile.close: An open door still asks you to walk through.

square.title: The Square

rows.t: It creates friction between two needs that both want attention.
You may feel pushed to act, to build, or to decide.
Pressure tends to become drive when you work with it.
Under transit, it often marks a turning point or a test.
Avoiding the conflict tends to make it return in new forms.
Over time, it can forge your strongest skills and resilience.

square.bridge: A square is friction that can become motion.
story: Ptolemy counts the square among his four configurations.
Ninety degrees: a quarter of the circle, signs three apart.
Its signs differ in gender yet share the same modality.
Ptolemy judged it disharmonious, a figure of strain.
Its figure is the square drawn within the zodiac.
square.close: What resists you may be what shapes you.

trine.title: The Trine

rows.t: It links planets in the same element; energy flows easily.
You may have talents that feel effortless, almost taken for granted.
Under transit, it tends to bring support, good timing, and grace.
Ease can turn into comfort that asks nothing of you.
Its gifts grow strongest when you consciously put them to use.
You tend to recover quickly where trines connect your chart.

trine.bridge: A trine is a gift; use keeps it alive.
story: Ptolemy counts the trine among his four configurations.
One hundred twenty degrees: a third of the circle.
It joins signs four apart, of the same triplicity.
He ranked it, with the sextile, as harmonious.
He grounded these figures in musical ratios of harmony.
trine.close: What comes easily still asks to be used well.

opposition.title: The Opposition

rows.t: Two planets face each other; you feel pulled in two directions.
You may meet one side of it through other people.
Relationships tend to mirror what you have not yet owned.
Under transit, it often brings matters to a visible peak.
Balance comes when you integrate both sides instead of choosing one.
Awareness is its gift; you learn yourself through the contrast.

opposition.bridge: An opposition shows you yourself from across the room.
story: Ptolemy counts the opposition among his four configurations.
One hundred eighty degrees: the diameter of the circle.
It joins signs six apart, facing across the zodiac.
The circle halved, 2 to 1: the ratio of the octave.
Ptolemy judged it disharmonious, a figure of contrast.
opposition.close: What stands opposite may be what completes you.

quincunx.title: The Quincunx

rows.t: It connects two planets that do not easily understand each other.
You may feel small adjustments are always needed between two areas.
There is no open conflict, just an awkward, persistent mismatch.
Under transit, it tends to ask for practical changes and recalibration.
Over time you learn flexibility, bridging what seems unrelated.
Ignoring it may leave a quiet sense that something is off.

quincunx.bridge: A quincunx asks you to adjust, not to choose.
story: A minor aspect of later astrology: 150 degrees.
It joins signs five apart, with nothing in common.
They share no element, no gender, no modality.
Hellenistic authors said such signs do not see each other.
Its Latin name means five twelfths of a whole.
Ptolemy's four figures do not include it.
quincunx.close: What does not fit may teach you to bend.
